hypothesis: If the claim holds, the primes below 10^8, generated by the sieve of Eratosthenes (the 'simple rule'), look random in most of a pre-declared list of statistical respects when compared with Cramer's random model (independent events with probability 1/ln n), while possibly showing structure in a minority of respects.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Generate all primes below N = 10^8 by sieve; validate against the OEIS A000040 b-file (first 10000 primes must match exactly) and the published value pi(10^8) = 5761455 (OEIS A006880). Simulate the Cramer model on the same range with numpy seed 20261031 and run every statistic on both. Seven respects, each with a threshold for 'random-like': R1 coarse gap distribution: for primes in [N/2, N], maximum over j of |F_emp(30 j) - (1 - exp(-30 j / mean gap))| < 0.03, where F_emp is the empirical CDF of gaps; R2 Pearson correlation of consecutive gaps in [N/2, N]: |rho| < 0.05; R3 equidistribution over the four residue classes coprime to 12: maximum deviation of a class share from 1/4 below 0.005 (the Cramer model is evaluated on its own coprime-to-12 events); R4 counts of primes in consecutive disjoint intervals of length H = round(ln N) in [N/2, N]: total variation distance between the empirical count distribution and Poisson with the same mean < 0.02; R5 discrete Fourier transform of the indicator of primes among the 2^22 odd numbers just below N: ratio of the largest non-zero-frequency power to the mean power < 30 (a Gumbel-scale maximum for random indicators is about ln(2^21) ~ 15); R6 sequential compressibility: lzma size of the sequence of half-gaps (clipped at 255) in [N/2, N] divided by the lzma size of a seeded random permutation of the same sequence >= 0.98; R7 maximum over x <= N of |pi(x) - Li(x)| / sqrt(x / ln x) < 3. A respect is calibrated only if the Cramer simulation satisfies its threshold; miscalibrated respects are dropped and reported. PASS (supports) if the primes are random-like in at least (K - 2) of the K calibrated respects (so 5 of 7 if all are calibrated).
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. FAIL (refutes) if the primes are random-like in at most K - 4 of the K calibrated respects (3 of 7), or if the gap sequence is plainly regular (lzma ratio of the raw half-gap byte sequence below 0.1, or a single Fourier frequency carrying more than half the non-DC spectral power). MIXED for exactly K - 3 random-like respects (4 of 7). If the OEIS validation fails the generator is wrong and the result is 'inconclusive' (other). If the OEIS files cannot be fetched, validation falls back to the published pi(10^8) value only and this is reported.
interpretation: The claim's testable core is 'their distribution seems in many respects random'; the historical remark about what mathematics neglected is not tested. 'Random' is given the book's own operational meaning (p. 1067 ff.: statistical indistinguishability from a random model in specified respects) with Cramer's model as the declared random model; 'many respects' is read as a majority of a list fixed in advance, which includes respects where structure is known to exist (Fourier peaks from small moduli, finite-size Poisson deviations) so that the test can fail. Trivial sieve structure (no even primes) is removed only in R3 by restricting to classes coprime to 12; all other statistics are applied to the raw sequences.

datasets.name: Primes below 10^8 from a sieve of Eratosthenes and a Cramer-model simulation on the same range, generated by analysis.py

generator.cramer: n in [3, 10^8) is 'prime' independently with probability 1/ln n, numpy default_rng(20261031); window statistics on [5x10^7, 10^8]
generator.window: [5x10^7, 10^8] for gap, interval and compression statistics; odd numbers in [10^8 - 2^23, 10^8) for the Fourier test
